The majority off the persons to be displaced by the Randolph Urban Renewal Program are black. At the time of the 100 percent survey three white families resided within the area.
The economic level of residents of the area range from the lower economic level to the professional with the lower economic level being in the majority in the area of greater density and dilapidation.
Relocation needs will therefore require resources for the low income, the elderly, moderate and higher price housing both sales and rentals.
With the provisions for and the availability of the Replacement Housing Payment to displaced persons, the intentions to stage displacement with the availability of new and rehabilitated units, the increasing amount of housing being produced within the City and the S.M.A., sufficient units are anticipated to become available to adequately rehouse site occupants displaced.
b. Elderly
There are 141 elderly families, 70 owners and 71 tenants, who will require relocation and 981 elderly individuals, including 167 owners and 814 tenants, who will require relocation. Most of these families and individuals are apparently eligible for public housing. The Richmond Redevelopment and Housing Authority presently operates 240 units of housing for the elderly. Priority for admission will be given to these families and individuals displaced. The first new housing to be undertaken in this program will provide housing for the elderly and elderly low-income housing units in other areas of the City are scheduled for completion within the next two years.
c. Large Families
The project will displace 37 families of 8 or more persons; 29 are eligible for public housing. Many of the larger families have indicated they intend to utilize the Replacement Housing Payments and purchase their relocation housing. Families eligible and desiring public housing can be accommodated.
